gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws a ruler-straight line with wide, unclosed curve endings. Plakkaat is the heavy one, its terminals curling nearly shut on the stem, while the sans-serif body is where the lines stay open and easy to follow.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-yaldevi: Yaldevi reads clean, its e opening clearly to the right and its lowercase running oversized. Yaldevi keeps that plain sans manner going line after line, while Plakkaat's heavy, nearly closed letters stay out of its way.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-abeezee: Quantum spaces its letters loosely, with open mouths and short ascenders that give it a tidy tech look. ABeeZee follows in sans-serif, its terminals finishing well clear of the stem and its line as rounded as neon glass tubing.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-aldrich: Aldrich reads like tracing one thick thread, with a tall lowercase nearly matching its capitals and rounds that look cupped. Quantum above it is lighter and looser, and that gap in texture is the strongest thing the pairing has going.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-alexandria: Quantum has a pen-plotter smoothness, with generous spacing between letters. It does best as the gliding display line, while Alexandria, a tall sans-serif with wide open terminals, does its best work as the steady text underneath.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-amiko: Crisp, cool and a touch futuristic. Amiko brings crayon-tall lowercase and terminals that flick outward like tongs, so Quantum's smooth, loosely spaced letters get a sturdier partner with more bite.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-bangla: Quantum glows like neon tube, one line thickness from end to end. Anek Bangla sits beside it in sans-serif, friendlier and more compact, with wide s curves that loosen the heading's techy precision.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari reads modern, with distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone. Over many lines that gives a sans body a smooth, unhurried flow, while Quantum's swell-free downstrokes keep the heading crisp above it.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-gujarati: Anek Gujarati reads friendly and clear, its lowercase rivaling the capitals and its c opening wide. Quantum is best at crisp, contrast-free display strokes; this sans-serif is best at carrying the text.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Quantum brings loose spacing and strokes with no calligraphic swelling anywhere. Anek Gurmukhi answers in sans-serif with big open counters and generous curves, and that shared openness is what makes the pair hang together.
